recipes.name: Crusted Salmon with Honey-Mustard Sauce
ingredients_raw: 1 (1.5 pound) skinless center-cut salmon fillet, cut into 4 pieces

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Coat a baking sheet with cooking spray; set aside.
Place fillets in a baking dish; pour milk on top and soak, 10 to 15 minutes.

Stir bread crumbs and Parmesan cheese together in a wide, shallow dish. Beat egg in a separate dish until frothy. Remove fillets from milk; shake off excess. Dip each fillet into egg, then gently press into bread crumb mixture to coat, shaking off excess. Arrange coated fillets on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until fillets easily flake with a fork, about 15 minutes, flipping halfway through.
Meanwhile, combine butter, mustard, and honey in a bowl; drizzle over fillets before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Crusted Salmon with Honey-Mustard Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This delightful salmon recipe crusts fillets with a breadcrumb-Parmesan mixture, bakes them, and then tops with a flavorful honey-mustard-butter sauce.

review.reviewBody: This is an excellent way of preparing salmon: the honey mustard sauce is a delicate complement to the flavor of the salmon. The sauce is neither too weak nor overpowers the fish. Also, it seems like the milk tenderizes the fish and mellows out the flavor slightly. Serve this with some rice pilaf and roasted veggies, and it looks like a very fancy meal without lots of fuss. Thanks for this recipe!!! My family has eaten this a few times already and have made sure to save it.

The only thing I changed is I soaked it for an hour in Bourbon before soaking in milk.I cooked them in a Ninja Foodi for 10 minutes at 350 with a thermometer. I used a thermometer and shut the ninja off at 138. The fillets were at 152 when I took them out. They were not overcooked and were still moist and tasty. I used Plochman's Stone Ground Craft Mustard. It added a wonderful taste that is both tangy and complex. It mixed well with the honey. This may be my best effort at cooking Salmon. This recipe is a keeper!

Normally I don't like toppings that overpower salmon, this didn't disappoint. It was a nice change that we both liked. I did hit the broiler for a few minutes to finish it off and lightly brown the top before serving. I used panko, fresh parm and added cayenne to give it a kick. Will have again, thank you!

Very Tasty I am not the biggest salmon eater but trying to incorporate it more in my diet. I followed the recipe mostly as written just tweaking it slightly per suggestions from other reviewers. I used a honey mustard mixture I already had prepared from a previous recipe which had some Coleman's mustard in it as I like my mustard with a little "kick." I also used panko crumbs and increased that and the parmesan to form a thicker crust. I also finished it off under the broiler to make a crunchy crust............. this was deeeeee-lish!!! melted in my mouth.

Absolutely delicious. I made few changes though. I did not use any milk to soak the salmon as I wanted to make a dairy-free version. In addition, I added some paprika, garlic powder, and salt to the bread crumb mixture before coating the salmon in it. Finally, I had no prepared bread crumbs at home so I toasted a slice of Oat & Honey bread, pulsed it in a food processor, toasted the bread crumbs some more in the oven, and threw it back in the food processor some more. This dish serves great with steamed veggies and rice!

This was a nice change of pace from our normal salmon recipes. I didn't use the egg and had no problem getting the bread crumbs to stick to the salmon. Definitely use panko for a lighter, crunchier fish. I cut the butter down to 2 tablespoons (and used light butter) but kept the honey and mustard the same. If your salmon is on the larger side (or even just wider and thinner), it might not be enough to cover 4 pieces. Pour the warmed sauce over top of the salmon and put back in the oven for a few minutes. It made for a nice meal (company worthy based on appearances) when served with savory whipped sweet potatoes and green beans with shallots and garlic.
I made it with the salmon and chicken breasts. I eliminated the salmon and the milk. It was delicious!

I made it as written using wild caught salmon that had a deep red color to the meat. It was outstanding. I paired it with angel hair pasta tossed with olive oil, fresh garlic and fresh grated parmesan. I also baked asparagus as the vegetable. My only caution is I felt like next time I'll double the bread crumb & cheese since I would have liked a bit more of that crust.

So easy and delicious! I’m always looking for a new way to cook salmon, and this was so simple. Loved the slight crunch which gave it a nice texture. Instead of making the honey mustard, I drizzled some mikes hot honey and just a small bit of mustard as soon as it came out of the oven. Really good!

I was a little skeptical of the unusual combination of Parmesan with honey mustard, but made this exactly as written and was quite surprised! You can barely taste the Parmesan, so it doesn't compete with the honey mustard sauce. Simple to make and perfect for weeknights. The only thing I suggest is cooking at a higher temp for a couple less minutes - the higher temp will get some color/browning on the salmon, as it turned out quite pale and I had to put it under the broiler for a minute to get it browned.

Bazinga! My new favorite. I prepared exactly as directed, except I heated the honey and mustard with the butter in order to make sure I wasn't pouring a cold glaze. Other than that, I would NOT change a thing. The bread crumbs and parmesan are important, I believe, as they soak up the yummy honey-mustard glaze. Thank you, Evan!
Didn't make any changes
Just needed a touch of vinegar on the fish as you were consuming it. Really, really added to the flavour.
The salmon was tender, cooked to perfection and the sauce was wonderful. I would definitely recommend this recipe.
😋 my mom and I love this salmon easy and delicious the sauce reminds me of Chick-fil-A honey mustard I will make this again
It was really yummy it was very yummy!
One of my favorite recipes for a quick prep and a tasty main dish. I often use this recipe in camp when salmon fishing in the Pacific NW. Good for steelhead also.
OMG - this recipe rocks salmon!
Oh. My God!!! This is a keeper….
I loved the Parmigiano cheese on it.and the honey mustard sauce is going to be used on something else as well.also this would be good on ling cod
